tour.overview:
Vatican City is the smallest independent state in the world, about 44 hectares behind its walls, yet it holds one of the richest art collections on earth and the largest church of Christianity. The popes began collecting ancient sculpture in 1506, when Julius II displayed the newly found Laocoön group, and over five centuries the Vatican Museums grew into some seven kilometres of galleries. The whole of Vatican City has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1984.

This private day takes you through the Vatican with a licensed guide who knows the shortest routes through the galleries. You enter the museums early with timed tickets, see the ancient sculptures of the Pio-Clementino, the Gallery of Maps and Raphael's Rooms, and reach the Sistine Chapel, where Michelangelo painted the ceiling between 1508 and 1512 and the Last Judgment more than twenty years later. You continue into St Peter's Basilica, then step out into Bernini's square. After lunch in the Prati district, you walk to Castel Sant'Angelo, the emperor Hadrian's tomb that became a papal fortress.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 7 hours 30 minutes
• Start and end: your hotel in Rome
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy; about 4 km, mostly indoors, with many stairs in the museums

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Vatican Museums: the Pio-Clementino, the Gallery of Candelabra, Tapestries and Maps.
• The Raphael Rooms.
• The Sistine Chapel.
• St Peter's Basilica and Michelangelo's Pietà.
• St Peter's Square.
• Castel Sant'Angelo and the Bridge of Angels (outside; the interior can be added).

WHY THIS WORKS
We book the first entry slots of the day and walk the museums in the order the crowds don't, so you reach the Sistine Chapel while it is still calm.

WHO IT SUITS
Art lovers, pilgrims, families and anyone visiting Rome who wants to understand what they are looking at in the Vatican.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If ancient Rome is your priority, choose our Colosseum, Roman Forum and Pantheon tour.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The museums are closed on Sundays, except the last Sunday of the month, and on many religious holidays. Shoulders and knees must be covered in the museums and the basilica. Photography is allowed in most galleries but not in the Sistine Chapel.

days.name: Vatican Museums, Raphael Rooms, Sistine Chapel, St Peter's Basilica and Castel Sant'Angelo
days.description:
What to expect: the treasures of the popes in one well-paced day, with a licensed guide, private car, timed tickets and lunch.

Your driver collects you at your hotel at about 7:45 and brings you to the walls of Vatican City, where your guide meets you for one of the first entries of the day. You start in the Pio-Clementino Museum with the masterpieces of ancient sculpture that inspired Renaissance artists: the Laocoön, found on the Esquiline Hill in 1506, the Apollo Belvedere and the muscular Belvedere Torso that Michelangelo studied. You walk through the Gallery of the Candelabra, the Gallery of Tapestries and the 120-metre Gallery of Maps, where painted frescoes show every region of Italy in the 1580s.

In the Raphael Rooms, painted for Pope Julius II, you stand in front of the School of Athens, with Plato, Aristotle and the young painter's own portrait among the philosophers. Then you enter the Sistine Chapel. Your guide explains the ceiling before you go in, because talking is not allowed inside: the Creation of Adam, the prophets and sibyls, and, on the altar wall, the Last Judgment painted by Michelangelo between 1536 and 1541. From the chapel, a passage leads straight into St Peter's Basilica when it is open, saving the walk around the walls.

Inside the basilica, rebuilt between 1506 and 1626 over the tomb of St Peter, you see Michelangelo's Pietà, carved when he was in his early twenties, Bernini's bronze canopy over the papal altar and the dome Michelangelo designed, rising 136 metres. You step out into St Peter's Square, embraced by Bernini's colonnade of 284 columns. After lunch in the Prati district, you walk down Via della Conciliazione to Castel Sant'Angelo and the Bridge of Angels, with Bernini's angels carrying the instruments of the Passion. Your driver takes you back to your hotel at about 15:30.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
07:45 – Pick-up at your hotel.
08:15 – Vatican Museums: sculpture galleries, Gallery of Maps.
09:45 – Raphael Rooms.
10:30 – Sistine Chapel.
11:15 – St Peter's Basilica.
12:15 – St Peter's Square.
12:45 – Lunch in Prati.
14:15 – Via della Conciliazione, Castel Sant'Angelo and the Bridge of Angels.
15:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The direct passage from the Sistine Chapel to the basilica is reserved for groups with a guide and can close without notice; we then walk around to the square.
• On Wednesdays the basilica is usually closed in the morning for the papal audience; we reorder the day.
• The dome climb (551 steps, or 320 after the lift) and the Castel Sant'Angelo interior can be added.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel tickets, guided basilica visit, lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: dome climb, Castel Sant'Angelo interior, drinks with lunch, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Do we skip the lines?
faq.answer: Yes. We book timed early-entry tickets, so you skip the ticket line, which can be over an hour long. There is a short security check for everyone.

faq.question: On which days is the tour not possible?
faq.answer: The Vatican Museums are closed on Sundays, except the last Sunday of each month, and on religious holidays such as Easter Monday, 29 June and Christmas. We suggest another day when you book.

faq.question: Is there a dress code?
faq.answer: Yes. Shoulders and knees must be covered for both men and women in the museums and the basilica. Sleeveless tops, shorts and short skirts can be refused at the entrance.

faq.question: Can we take photos in the Sistine Chapel?
faq.answer: No. Photos and videos are not allowed in the Sistine Chapel, and silence is requested. Photography without flash is allowed in most other galleries and in the basilica.

faq.question: Is there much walking?
faq.answer: About 4 km, mostly indoors on marble floors, with many stairs in the museums. There are lifts for those who need them.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, lunch at a local restaurant in the Prati district. Vegetarian, gluten-free and other diets can be arranged.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. We keep the stories lively, look for animals and maps in the galleries, and can shorten the museum part for younger children.

faq.question: Is it suitable for wheelchair users?
faq.answer: Largely. The museums have a wheelchair route with lifts, and wheelchairs can be borrowed free of charge. The basilica is accessible. Tell us in advance so we plan the route.

faq.question: Can we climb the dome of St Peter's?
faq.answer: Yes, it can be added. There is a lift to the roof terrace, then 320 narrow steps to the top. It is not suitable for people with heart conditions or claustrophobia.

faq.question: Can we see the Pope?
faq.answer: On most Wednesdays the Pope holds a general audience in St Peter's Square, and on Sundays he recites the Angelus at noon. Free audience tickets can be requested; we can adapt the day.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: October to March is quieter. In spring and summer, the early entry makes the biggest difference. The museums are busiest on the free last Sunday and on Mondays and Saturdays.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 72 hours before the tour, because Vatican tickets are non-refundable after that. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
